chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad from Ahmad from Mufaddal ibn Salih from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one who fasted the Day of Tarwiyah and the Day of Arafah, he said: 'It suffices him that he fasts another day.'

key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: It suffices him / It is accepted as valid

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting the Day of Tarwiyah and Day of Arafah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the phrase 'yujzihi an yasuma yawman akhara' is interpreted by Shia jurists to mean that fasting on these specific days of Dhul-Hijjah serves as a valid substitute or discharge for a missed obligatory fast (Qada), rather than merely being a voluntary reward. This highlights the high spiritual merit of fasting during the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, particularly the Day of Arafah, which is often cited as expiating sins for the preceding and coming year. The ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the interchangeability of voluntary and obligatory fasts when specific conditions are met.
